I'll review the implemented scope from the diff, contract, and qualification summary, then check the seven changed paths for concrete security and correctness defects.**High.** `exists` whose body is `any(...)` is fail-open: the relation key is OR-ed with the disjunction, so one matching related row makes the predicate true for every outer row.

`PredicateCompiler::compile` gives every `any` operand boolean `or`, including the first (`packages/core/src/Authorization/Query/PredicateCompiler.php` lines 70–73). `exists` compiles that tree directly onto the `whereHas` builder (lines 89–94), which already has the correlation (`whereColumn`, boolean `and`). Eloquent then keeps that leading `or` as the link to the key (`Builder::callScope` / `groupWhereSliceForScope`). The subquery is `key = parent OR (disjuncts)`, not `key = parent AND (disjuncts)`.

Trigger: `exists('project', any(eq('active', true)))`, and the same shape on dotted paths (`project.members`), self-relations (`parent`), nested `exists`, and `exists(rel, any(branch(...), branch(...)))`. A single related row with `active = true` makes `EXISTS` true for every resource, including `project_id` null. On a self-relation, one row that satisfies the `any` admits the whole table. OR of contribution branches is not held inside the typed relation.

Root-level `any` is unaffected: it is compiled onto an empty nested group that is AND-ed to the host. `all`, `not`, `branch`, and `in` (NULL handled inside an AND group) stay correlated. V1 does not cover `exists` + `any`.

NULL complements, host WHERE grouping, identifier checks before `delete`/`save`, atomic unsupported siblings, policy allow/deny/abstain versus before deny/pass, branch identity, and bindings match the contract. Unsupported MorphTo, cross-connection, and aliased FROM paths are rejected as specified.

VERDICT: FINDINGS
